column1: # Entering a container's or another process's namespaces is a second door to `incus exec`/`incus shell`, which the
# deny hook refuses outright (a mutating verb, read-only commands included). With passwordless sudo it opens a root
# shell inside a container (attic's, which holds the cache's signing and token secrets), whatever is run there. So it
# is refused the same way, outright, not by what it launches (🛡️, 2026-10-25, after 🎛️ routed a refused incus exec
# through nsenter). Columns, tab-separated: want (DENY|ALLOW), today (2c8c188e's hook, measured), cwd (- for /tmp/work),
# cmd. A case is loosened only with 🛡️'s review.
# nsenter, by any of its forms, read-only commands included (as incus exec is). A bare `sh` launched this way is
# already refused by the root-shell rule (2c8c188e), by side effect; a read-only command (`ss`, `cat`) is not.
# Its relatives: other ways into a container or a namespace.
# Already refused, kept so a rewrite keeps them: the front door.
# Reading about them, or listing, changes nothing.
